text: Occupation: Local Business Owner

Manhattan Beach has a big spending problem, not a revenue problem. The current Council is spending irresponsibly and adding more expensive positions like a Deputy City Manager which we eliminated the last time I was on Council. Our reserves are being spent down and projects like the Senior/Scout House aren't getting done.

NO Matter how this council tries to "spin it" they have spent the full $4 million in economic uncertainty reserves and $7.0 million from additional reserves. It's also pushed "pause" on paying into the city's pension trust fund or contributing to the city's infrastructure reserves that will further delay important projects.

When I left Council in 2024, a sales tax increase (added $6.5 million) along with an increased stormwater fee boosted City revenue. We never dipped into reserves and we did not stop investing in our infrastructure.

But somehow, we've gone from financial stability to financial crisis in two short years! This is no way to run a city! As mayor during the Great Recession and again during Covid, I offer proven crisis leadership.
Our current council has dug us into a fiscal hole, and they keep digging! This has to stop. If you elect me, it will.

text: Age: 61
Occupation: Incumbent

I'm running for City Council to use my twenty years of elected experience as both a MBUSD Trustee and City Councilmember to navigate future challenges while preserving our small beach town character. I've worked hard to build consensus, earn trust, and deliver for our residents.

Sacramento's housing mandates raise real concerns about impacts to our quality of life. Among other mitigation strategies, I supported the City's first residential developer fees to alleviate stress on our infrastructure and will keep pressuring state representatives to seek legislative changes.

Public safety remains a priority. I backed hiring seven additional police officers, a drone first responder program, saw the completion of Fire Station 2, and secured funding for critical Sepulveda Boulevard safety improvements. I will continue advocating for sensible E bike legislation and enforcement.
Our local small businesses are vital to our community. I've championed solutions that support them, such as the Circuit Waverider, expansion of our beloved Farmers Market, and free holiday parking.
I'm running for City Council because I love Manhattan Beach, and after two decades of service, I know how to serve it well.
I ask for your vote on November 3rd.
Thank You!
See amyhoworth.net to learn more.

text: Occupation: Attorney
Dear Neighbor,
I am seeking a 2nd term to the City Council to continue putting the residents of Manhattan Beach always first.

Our community deserves a government that listens to the people-not special interests. With a proven record of fighting to ensure city business was conducted with absolute transparency, I remain deeply committed to that mission while demanding fiscal accountability that reduces wasteful spending by 10% and protects our local tax dollars.
- Protect Our Small-Town Character: Stop high-rise developments; defend local zoning control; and protect our neighborhoods from severe traffic and infrastructure strain.
- Restore Fiscal Accountability: We must end irresponsible deficit spending.
- Implement Strict Term Limits Local: Government thrives on new ideas, not entrenched power. Two four-year terms is enough.

Having served as your former Mayor and Councilmember, alongside a career as a Senior Assistant City Attorney for the City of Los Angeles, I understand municipal law and how city government works...how to deliver tangible results, manage balanced budgets, and provide the collaborative leadership our community deserves to ensure Manhattan Beach remains a safe, beautiful, and thriving place to live.
With a lifelong career dedicated to public service, I
respectfully ask for your vote by November 3rd.
Thank you.

text: Age: 57
Occupation: Retired Publicist

I moved to Manhattan Beach 12 years ago, after retiring from a successful career in Strategic Communications in DC and New York City. Since moving here, I have volunteered and advocated for MB Neighborhood Watch, the Friends of Polliwog Park and our Botanical Garden. I also served on the Planning Commission for 7 years and share the concerns of residents regarding over development and state overreach.

If elected, my priorities will be instituting hard term limits for City Council, balancing the budget, restoring a culture of saving for deferred maintenance of our aging city buildings and infrastructure, and increasing the visibility of our current Police force. Additionally, I am committed to ending the 5-0 voting, "go along to get along" status quo on our council that does not accurately represent the diversity of opinions and priorities among the residents of our community.

As a leadership trainer and a civic minded resident, I firmly believe in putting my skills and experience at the service of my community and that a finite term fosters urgency, innovation and, ultimately, results. I would be honored to serve my fellow residents as we improve our community for the next generation of residents and local leaders.
